text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 3.2% today, extending a two-week decline of 9%. The most concrete trigger appears to be U.S. crude oil falling below $95 per barrel on November 3rd—the same day the company reported quarterly earnings—after diplomatic signals suggested the Iran conflict may be resolved without further escalation. Lower oil prices directly squeeze refiner margins, since they buy crude and sell refined products like gasoline and diesel; when oil gets cheaper faster than end-product prices fall, profit shrinks. While refineries are running near full capacity (92.8%), that high utilization can't offset the headwind from collapsing crude costs.

The stock's broader weakness over two weeks also reflects investor caution ahead of Big Oil earnings season. A leadership change and company update announced on October 29th landed as analysts were already warning that guidance—not just current earnings—would drive sentiment, suggesting the market is worried less about today's results than tomorrow's outlook in an environment where oil prices are volatile and geopolitical risk is shifting.
